title: Admin menu moved out of the way, and every outbound link documented
summary: Two changes aimed at fitting into WordPress rather than competing with it: the plugin's top-level menu no longer sits above Appearance, and the readme now lists the external pages its admin screens link to.
changes: Changed: the plugin's top-level admin menu now sits between Tools and Settings instead of directly above Appearance. Nothing else about the menu changes -- the same screens are in the same order underneath it -- but it no longer pushes past WordPress's own items.

Docs: the readme's "External services" section now lists every page outside your site that the admin screens link to (the documentation site, the issue tracker, wpalemi.com with its terms and privacy pages, this plugin's WordPress.org support forum, the wp-mail-smtp and fluent-smtp plugin pages, and a YouTube channel). The plugin still makes no request to any of them -- these are links a user may click. A build check guards against reintroducing the third-party services earlier versions used (geolocation, CDN fonts and scripts, analytics, Gravatar).
notice: No action required. If you navigate by muscle memory, the MHM Rentiva menu is now lower down the admin sidebar, just above Settings.

title: A table definition WordPress could not read
summary: The background-job table was created with a statement WordPress's schema updater cannot read, which would have made any later change to that table silently fail to apply. Fixed, and the readme's Privacy section has been corrected and expanded.
changes: Fixed: the background-job table was created with "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS". WordPress reads the words after CREATE TABLE as the table's name, so its schema updater had been tracking a table called "IF" — a table it cannot describe, and therefore skipped entirely. The real table was created correctly by the database itself and no data was lost, but any column added to it in a later release would silently never have been applied. Measured on a live database: before the fix a newly added column was ignored; after it, the same column was created. Existing tables are updated in place and no data is touched.

Docs: the readme's Privacy section has been corrected. It now discloses that every contact-form submission is stored with the sender's name, e-mail, telephone, message and the IP address and browser user-agent it came from, and that those records have no retention setting at all. It also notes that reviews left through the rating form are stored as WordPress comments, so WordPress records the reviewer's IP with them, and describes what the activity log and the e-mail log each hold and how long they keep it, and states that bookings placed through WooCommerce checkout record no IP address. What the plugin stores has not changed; the description of it was incomplete.
notice: No action required. No column is pending for this table, so nothing changes on your site today; the fix is what makes the next schema change to it actually apply.

title: WooCommerce compatibility, declared and corrected
summary: The plugin now answers WooCommerce's compatibility questions instead of leaving them blank, and one piece of order data is written through the order object so it is correct on both storage layouts.
changes: Fixed: the plugin now tells WooCommerce which of its storage features it works with. Without that declaration WooCommerce could not confirm compatibility, and site owners turning on High-Performance Order Storage — the default for new stores since WooCommerce 8.2 — were warned about this plugin by name.

Fixed: the payment type chosen at checkout was written to order storage in a way that only works on the older layout. It is now written through WooCommerce's own order object, so it lands in the right place whichever storage a store uses. On existing stores the value stays exactly where it has always been; nothing is moved and nothing needs migrating.

Declared: this plugin is NOT compatible with the block-based cart and checkout, and now says so instead of leaving it unanswered. On a block checkout the payment-type selector, the custom tax row and the return-to-cart link do not appear, and — the part that matters most — the availability check that prevents two customers booking the same vehicle for the same dates does not run. Use the classic checkout with this plugin.
notice: No action required and nothing to migrate. If your store uses the block-based checkout, note the third item: switch to the classic checkout to keep the availability check and the payment-type selector.

title: Truthful dashboard chart label, and translations that actually ship
summary: The dashboard revenue chart was named after something it does not measure, and five admin strings shipped in English despite being translated. Both are fixed, and the translation build that caused the second one is now checked on every push.
changes: Fixed: the dashboard chart was labelled "Revenue (Last 7 Days)" but sums the value of bookings CREATED in those days, not rental income earned in them — which is why it could read as empty while the table beside it listed upcoming rentals. It is now "New Bookings Value (Last 7 Days)", and the daily series is "Daily Bookings Value". The figures themselves are unchanged.

Fixed: five admin strings were translated but shipped in English, because the React translation catalogues could not be regenerated and the stale ones were four months old. Affects "Pending Payments", "Upcoming Operations", their empty-state messages, and the notice shown if an admin screen fails to load.
Removed: eleven translation catalogues belonging to screens and blocks that are no longer part of this plugin. Nothing loaded them.
Docs: the readme now lists Chart.js among the bundled third-party libraries, with its version, licence and upstream source.

Internal: the translation-catalogue build is deterministic again, and a continuous-integration check now fails if the shipped catalogues fall out of step with the translation source instead of silently going stale.
notice: No action required. Only wording and translations changed; no figure, setting or stored data is affected.

title: Security hardening and redesigned admin screens
summary: Permission checks now test the specific booking or vehicle a request names rather than a general capability, and plugin-generated markup is filtered as it is printed. The Dashboard and Vehicle Settings screens have been redesigned.
changes: Security: booking, deposit, vehicle-gallery and blocked-date handlers check the caller against the specific record the request names, instead of a general "can edit content" capability. On multi-author sites this closes paths where one contributor could act on another contributor’s bookings, galleries or availability.
Security: saving a booking from the editor now always requires a valid security token; the presence of a form field is no longer accepted in its place.
Security: the database backup screen exports, restores and deletes only backup tables created by this plugin. Other tables in the database can no longer be named in those requests.
Security: markup the plugin generates is filtered through an explicit allowlist as it is printed, replacing places that relied on the output having been escaped earlier.
Removed a booking-status endpoint and the script that called it: neither had an interface and the endpoint performed no action.
Fixed: the translation catalogue now compiles without errors. Strings containing placeholders such as %days% were mis-flagged as printf formats.
New: redesigned Dashboard and Vehicle Settings screens. Vehicle Settings opens in the new layout by default; add ?ui=legacy to the page URL to use the previous one for this release.

Removed the Settings → Security tab. Its seventeen controls — "Brute Force Protection", "SQL Injection Protection", "XSS Protection", "CSRF Protection", "Enable Rate Limiting" and the IP lists — were not connected to anything: switching them on changed nothing. A control that says a protection is active while nothing enforces it is worse than no control at all, because it gets relied on. The saved values are cleaned up automatically when you update.

Removed the "Secure API Access Tokens" section from Integration settings. It issued keys labelled READ, WRITE and ADMIN, but no part of the plugin ever checked them — a key created there opened nothing. Stored keys are removed when you update. The REST API itself is unchanged and still authenticates normally.
Removed the Integration settings that were also not wired to anything: token duration, token refresh, API caching, debug output and "Allow Global CORS". Rate limiting, which does work, stays.

Removed the "Scheduled Notifications" background job. It ran every hour on a queue that no part of the plugin ever added anything to, and the Cron Monitor reported it as healthy. Booking confirmations, reminders and refund notices are sent by the e-mail system and are unaffected.
Fixed: choosing "delete all data on uninstall" stopped partway through. Removing the plugin left tables, scheduled jobs and taxonomy terms behind even though the setting was on.
Fixed: the database backups screen could go blank. Any .sql file in the backup folder without a matching database record triggered a fatal error while the list was being built.
Database backups are now written under your uploads folder instead of directly into wp-content. Backups taken by earlier versions stay listed, restorable and deletable — nothing is moved or lost.

Fixed: vehicle quick edit accepted values the full vehicle editor rejects. A daily price could be saved as a negative number, which then multiplied into rental totals, and the seat count could be set to zero or above the configured maximum.

Fixed: the vehicle search request accepted any page size, so a single request could ask the site to render the whole fleet. Search and testimonials now cap the page size at the limit their own settings advertise.

Internal: temporary cache entries, the user's last-login record, background job names and the JavaScript objects our admin screens read now all carry the plugin's own prefix, so they cannot collide with another plugin storing something under the same name. Caches simply expire and are rebuilt. The last-login value is written under the new name from this version on; the old entry is left untouched, because that name is shared with other plugins and is not ours to delete, and the customer dashboard reads whichever exists.

Internal: removed around 2,000 lines of code that nothing referenced, including one file that registered database-maintenance commands and one that would have exposed protected vehicle and booking fields over the REST API if it had ever been switched on.

Removed the "Add Vehicle" control from the vehicle comparison. It was connected to nothing: the button had no handler, the endpoints behind it were never registered, and the Elementor switch that claimed to turn it on or off had no effect either way. Selecting a vehicle and pressing the button did nothing at all.

Fixed: "Auto Cleanup Logs" and "Log Retention (Days)" were ignored by the daily log purge, which always deleted entries older than thirty days — permanently, not to the trash — even with cleanup switched off or retention set higher. It now reads the settings you actually saved.
Fixed: saving the Vehicle settings tab silently reset "Vehicles per page" and "Default sort order" on the Frontend tab, two fields the Vehicle tab does not display.
Fixed: the dashboard's recent-bookings panel could stay up to twelve hours out of date after a booking changed, because its cache was cleared under a name the cache no longer used.
Fixed: the customers screen re-ran its full set of queries on every load. Its caching was requesting a cache type that had never been registered, so nothing was ever stored or read.

Internal: every script and stylesheet the plugin registers now carries its full prefix, so it cannot be displaced by another plugin registering the same short name — WordPress keeps whichever was registered first and discards the other without warning.
Internal: settings saved from an unrecognised tab are no longer written to the database unchecked.
notice: No action required. Site administrators are unaffected by the permission changes; on sites with editor or author roles, those users can now only act on records they are entitled to.

title: WordPress.org compliance hardening
summary: Internal compliance and code-hygiene pass ahead of the WordPress.org listing. No feature or behaviour change.
changes: Internal: the REST API-key and deposit-management AJAX actions now use the full mhm_rentiva_ prefix, and a duplicate registration of the API-key handlers was removed so each action is handled exactly once.

Internal: removed a leftover reference to a settings class that is not part of the free plugin, unreachable deposit-calculation code, and developer debug logging from the block-editor and search scripts.

Internal: the customer privacy controls now render only when their handlers are available (they ship with the paid add-on), so the free plugin shows no non-functional buttons; add-on-only scripts were also removed from the free plugin.
Docs: the readme describes the bundled shared UI library with neutral wording.
notice: No action required; your settings and data are unaffected.

title: Security and WordPress.org compliance
summary: Security hardening and WordPress.org guideline compliance. The free plugin's features and behaviour are unchanged; this release tightens input, output and capability handling, removes the bundled demo-data tool, and documents the source code.
changes: Security: contact-form attachment paths are resolved through WordPress upload APIs with containment checks, closing a file-path handling issue.
Security: creating a customer WordPress account now requires the create_users capability, and REST routes are gated on the matching user-management capability.
Security: additional output escaping, settings array-key sanitization and public query-variable registration across the admin and frontend.
Changed: testimonial and account avatars now render locally from initials, with no external Gravatar request; the plugin makes no third-party calls.
Removed: the demo-data seeder and its bundled sample images are no longer part of the plugin.
Added: a Source code section in the readme documenting the React build and the public repository.
Internal: the paid add-on now attaches only through neutral WordPress hooks; the free plugin ships no licensing or paid-feature scaffolding.
notice: No action required; your settings and data are unaffected.

title: WordPress.org compliance hardening
summary: Housekeeping for the WordPress.org listing. The plugin's features are unchanged; these are prefix, menu-placement and translation-extraction improvements plus removal of an internal developer tool.
changes: Changed: the admin menu now sits lower in the WordPress menu instead of near the top, so it no longer competes with core items.
Fixed: about 105 error and status messages were previously not extractable for translation; they are now proper gettext calls and fully translated to Turkish.
Changed: internal AJAX action names on the Vehicle Settings screen are now plugin-prefixed.
Removed: a developer-only diagnostics test runner that used to ship with the plugin.
Internal: prepared-statement queries annotated to silence false-positive scanner warnings; the paid add-on's email templates now ship with the add-on.
notice: No action required; existing settings and data are unaffected.

title: Export screen fixes (shared bundle) and translation update
summary: Fixes to a shared React admin bundle that the separate Rentiva add-on registers. The free plugin has no export screen, so its behaviour is unchanged.
changes: Fixed: the export screen's Export button posted its security nonce under the field name "nonce", but the handler verifies with check_admin_referer(), which reads _wpnonce — so every export, CSV included, failed with a "the link you followed has expired" error. It is now posted as _wpnonce.
New: the export history table shows which format (CSV or JSON) each entry was exported as.
i18n: Turkish translation updated for the new export-screen strings.
Docs: expanded the README.md and README-tr.md feature overview (GitHub only; neither file ships in the plugin ZIP).
notice: The free plugin's behaviour is unchanged; no action required.

title: First public WordPress.org release
summary: MHM Rentiva's first release on WordPress.org: the complete rental core with no artificial limits, no third-party requests, and full WordPress.org coding-standards compliance. Every screen works exactly as before — this release changes how the plugin is packaged and loaded, not what it does.
changes: New: First public release on WordPress.org — fleet management, availability, bookings, customers, WooCommerce payments, email notifications and the customer account pages, with no vehicle, booking or listing caps, no feature timers and no locked screens.
Compliance: the plugin makes no third-party requests at all — the webfont is bundled and served from your own site, and there are no geolocation, analytics or CDN calls.

Compliance: every admin and front-end script and style now loads through the WordPress asset system (wp_enqueue) instead of inline <script>/<style> blocks, with no change to how any screen looks or behaves.
Security: the separate add-on's features now attach only through the free plugin's neutral extension points, closing paths where they could otherwise run unintentionally.
16 shortcodes, 16 Gutenberg blocks and 17 Elementor widgets share a single renderer (Render Parity) so all three produce identical output. Ships with a full Turkish translation.
notice: First WordPress.org release. If you are upgrading from a pre-release build, no action is required.
